templates.pattern: Light travels from air into a medium at a speed of [V] × 10⁶ m/s. What is the refractive index of the medium? (c = 3 × 10⁸ m/s)
Light travels from air into glass of refractive index [N]. The angle of incidence is [AI] degrees. Using Snell's law (sin i = n × sin r), which value is closest to sin of the angle of refraction?
templates.explanation: Snell's law: sin r = sin i ÷ n. sin [AI]° ÷ [N] gives the sin of refraction angle.

templates.pattern:
A glass block has refractive index [N]. Using sin C = 1 ÷ n, what is the critical angle?
A) 30°  B) 42°  C) 48°  D) 60°
templates.explanation: sin C = 1 ÷ n. For n=[N], sin C = 1÷[N], giving C = [RESULT]. Beyond this angle total internal reflection occurs.

templates.pattern: An object is placed [U] cm from a converging lens of focal length [F] cm. Using the lens formula, what is the image distance v in cm?
An image is formed [V] cm from a lens and the object is [U] cm from the lens. What is the magnification produced?
templates.explanation: Magnification = image distance ÷ object distance = [V] ÷ [U] = [RESULT]. A value greater than 1 means the image is larger than the object.

templates.pattern:
A ray of light travels inside glass and hits the glass-air boundary. The critical angle of the glass is [C] degrees. If the angle of incidence is [A] degrees, what happens?
A) The ray refracts out into air
B) Total internal reflection occurs
C) The ray is absorbed
D) The ray slows down and stops
options: A) The ray refracts out into air
D) The ray slows down and stops
answer_label: A) The ray refracts out into air
A) The ray refracts out into air
templates.explanation: Critical angle = [C]°. Angle of incidence = [A]°. If [A]° > [C]°, total internal reflection occurs. If [A]° < [C]°, the ray refracts out into air.

templates.pattern: A converging lens of focal length [F] cm produces an image [V] cm from the lens. What is the object distance in cm?
templates.explanation: Lens formula rearranged: u = vF ÷ (v−F) = [V]×[F] ÷ ([V]−[F]) = [V*F] ÷ [V-F] = [RESULT] cm

templates.pattern: An object [H] cm tall is magnified [M] times by a lens. What is the height of the image in cm?
templates.explanation: Image height = object height × magnification = [H] × [M] = [RESULT] cm

templates.pattern:
Light travels from medium 1 (refractive index [N1]) into medium 2 (refractive index [N2]), where [N2] is less than [N1]. Which statement is correct?
A) Light speeds up and bends away from the normal
B) Light slows down and bends toward the normal
C) Light speed stays the same
D) Light is totally internally reflected
options: A) Light speeds up and bends away from the normal
B) Light slows down and bends toward the normal
C) Light speed stays the same
D) Light is totally internally reflected
answer_label: A) Light speeds up and bends away from the normal
A) Light speeds up and bends away from the normal
A) Light speeds up and bends away from the normal
A) Light speeds up and bends away from the normal
templates.explanation: Moving from higher n ([N1]) to lower n ([N2]) means speed increases (v = c÷n). Light bends away from the normal when entering a less dense medium.

templates.pattern: A lens has a power of [P] dioptres. What is its focal length in cm?
templates.explanation: Power (dioptres) = 1 ÷ focal length (metres). Focal length = 1 ÷ [P] m = 100 ÷ [P] cm = [RESULT] cm
